issues.why: Missing critical caveat: Dutch oven MUST be preheated empty before baking; baking cold dough in a cold pot produces flat dense bread, not the claimed results.

Factual error: isoamyl acetate is an acetate ester, not an estolide. Estolides are fatty acid dimers — categorically different compounds; the atom id name 'estolide_compounds' is wrong in this context.

Misleading universal framing: 75-80F is presented as the target regardless of conditions, but many experienced bakers deliberately target 68-72F for cooler long ferments; a beginner following this as a rule would over-ferment on the counter.

Missing load-bearing caveat: steam in the first 20 minutes of baking keeps the crust flexible so the loaf can expand; the definition describes crust formation chemistry but never warns that insufficient steam = no spring = ruined crumb regardless of correct temperature.

Oversimplified: 450-500F is the initial temperature, but most sourdough schedules drop to 400-425F after the first 20 minutes for even crumb bake-through; a user baking at 500F for the full duration will get burned crust and raw interior.

Misleading framing: listing 'alcohols for aroma' implies alcohols contribute meaningfully to bread aroma, but the vast majority of ethanol evaporates during baking; the aromatic contribution of alcohols in finished bread is negligible compared to acids and esters.
